learn.title: Where geometry starts
learn.body: Geometry is the study of shape, size and position. It starts from three simple ideas that we do not define with other words: a point, a line and a plane. Every other figure in this course is built from them.

learn.title: Point, line, plane
learn.body: A point is an exact location with no size. A line is perfectly straight and goes on forever in both directions. A plane is a flat surface that goes on forever, like a floor with no walls. Points are named with capital letters, such as $A$ and $B$.

learn.title: Segment and ray
learn.body: A segment is the part of a line between two endpoints, so it has a length. A ray starts at one point and goes on forever in one direction. Ray $AB$ starts at $A$ and passes through $B$. Points on the same line are collinear.

learn.title: Add segments
learn.body: If $B$ is between $A$ and $C$ on a line, then $AB+BC=AC$.
Two different points lie on exactly one line. Three points that are not on one line lie in exactly one plane.

questions.prompt: How many lines pass through two different points?
questions.explanation: Two points fix a straight line. You cannot draw a second straight line through both.

questions.prompt: Which figure has exactly one endpoint?
questions.explanation: A ray starts at a point and goes on forever one way. A segment has two endpoints and a line has none.
A segment is the part of a line between two endpoints. A ray has one and a line has none.

questions.prompt: Three points on the same line are called what?
questions.explanation: Collinear means lying on one line. Points on one plane are coplanar, which is a different idea.

questions.prompt: Match each figure to its description.
questions.explanation: Point, segment, ray and line differ in how many endpoints they have and whether they have size or length.
